newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's BA/American decision in weeks, not months.
newsitem.headline: EU's BA/American decision in weeks, not months.

text.p: The European Commission will take a final decision in weeks rather than months on the proposed alliance between British Airways and American Airlines, Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock said on Tuesday.

Asked by Reuters as he left a meeting of the European Parliament transport committee if it would take the Commission weeks or months to reach its decision, he said: "It's not months, it's not far away. But it's all complicated by the need to look at five alliances."
Kinnock shares responsibility with Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert for assessing the transatlantic air alliance on which the Commission has expressed strong competition concerns.
The Commission is also looking at planned alliances involving Lufthansa, SAS, United Airlines, KLM, Northwest , Sabena, Swissair, Delta Air Lines and Austrian Airlines .
Van Miert told Reuters as he arrived at the parliament to speak to the committee that the final decision would take "at least a month".
He said he was expecting to consult national experts from the EU states on the issue "within weeks".
Van Miert told the committee Britain and the Commission were still far part on how to deal with the planned alliance.
"Contact has resumed (between the Commission and the UK authorities) but positions still differ widely on the substance of the case," he said.
Van Miert said he was waiting for British Airways and AMR'S American Airlines to provide "supplementary information" on their proposed alliance.
This was on top of written and oral answers given by the two companies to the Commission's objections about the deal, he said in a text released ahead of his speech.
Only then would the Commission be able to consult national experts of the EU's 15 states before reaching a final decision, Van Miert said. He did not say what additional information he required.
